newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sniper attack heats up Nicaragua election dispute.
newsitem.headline: Sniper attack heats up Nicaragua election dispute.

text.p: Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman on Monday called on left-wing Sandinista rival Daniel Ortega to rein in his supporters after a sniper opened fire on a caravan of Aleman followers, injuring two.

The attack took place late on Saturday in Matagalpa, about 80 miles (130 km) north of Managua, as a caravan of Aleman's Liberal Alliance party toured the streets celebrating victory in the disputed Oct. 20 elections, police said.
"The investigation is under way, but we still have made no arrests," police spokesman Justo Zamora told Reuters.
The two injured Liberal supporters, Antonio Zacarias Orozco and Alvaro Santiago Sanchez, remain under observation in a local hospital after being shot in the chest and jaw, respectively, Zamora said.

Aleman linked the attack to the Sandinistas, who have protested his election win as fraudulent, and said the shooting came in the context of "the violent language of the Sandinista leaders and the Sandinista media."
"Commander Ortega should make a call to his followers to avoid tragedies of greater scope that cause more suffering and pain to our people," Aleman said in a statement.
The left-wing Sandinista Front also condemned the attack, calling the gunman a "criminal."
"The Sandinista Front, we repeat, rejects such methods as obsolete and criminal," an editorial in the Sandinista-owned newspaper Barricada said.
The Sandinistas have legally appealed for new elections to be held in the departments (provinces) of Managua and Matagalpa.
Their rebellion against the vote's results has sparked fears of post-election violence as angry Sandinista activists protest alleged Liberal fraud.
Local newspapers reported people shouting "Liberal tamales!" at the caravan before the shooting. Tamal is Nicaraguan slang for thief.
The CSE is scheduled to rule on the Sandinista appeal later in the week.
Barring a successful Sandinista appeal, Aleman, the anti-Sandinista former mayor of Managua, will don the presidential sash on Jan. 10.
